\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{যোগব্যায়াম} (jogbyāyām)}{যোগব্যায়াম (jogbyāyām)}]{\bn{যোগব্যায়াম} (jogbyāyām) — yoga (as exercise)}

\label{lesson:BN-C522-jogbyayam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a catch in cricket, then the Bengali for to hit hard.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{যোগব্যায়াম}}
\textbf{\bn{যোগব্যায়াম}} — \emph{jogbyāyām} — \textquotedblleft{}yoga (as exercise)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{দাদু} \bn{রোজ} \bn{সকালে} \bn{যোগব্যায়াম} \bn{করেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dādu roj sôkāle jogbyāyām kôren.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandfather does yoga every morning.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{যোগব্যায়াম}} (\emph{jogbyāyām}) joins Sanskrit \emph{yoga}, \textquotedblleft{}joining, discipline\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{vyāyāma}, \textquotedblleft{}exertion, struggle\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams); \bn{ব্যায়াম} on its own is exercise.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jogbyāyām}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jogbyāyām}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Dādu roj sôkāle jogbyāyām kôren.} — My grandfather does yoga every morning.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a catch in cricket, then the Bengali for to hit hard, then say \emph{jogbyāyām} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{যোগব্যায়াম} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Yoga (as exercise)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{পালোয়ান} (pāloyān)}{পালোয়ান (pāloyān)}]{\bn{পালোয়ান} (pāloyān) — a strongman; a wrestler (in the old style)}

\label{lesson:BN-C522-paloyan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to hit hard, then the Bengali for yoga.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{পালোয়ান}}
\textbf{\bn{পালোয়ান}} — \emph{pāloyān} — \textquotedblleft{}a strongman; a wrestler (in the old style)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{গ্রামের} \bn{পালোয়ান} \bn{একাই} \bn{একটা} \bn{ভারী} \bn{পাথর} \bn{তুলল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Grāmer pāloyān ekāi ekṭā bhārī pāthôr tullô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The village strongman lifted a heavy stone all by himself.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{পালোয়ান}} (\emph{pāloyān}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{pahlavān}, \textquotedblleft{}a champion, a hero\textquotedblright{}, worn down in everyday speech.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pāloyān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pāloyān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Grāmer pāloyān ekāi ekṭā bhārī pāthôr tullô.} — The village strongman lifted a heavy stone all by himself.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to hit hard, then the Bengali for yoga, then say \emph{pāloyān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{পালোয়ান} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A strongman; a wrestler (in the old style)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ফিট} (phiṭ)}{ফিট (phiṭ)}]{\bn{ফিট} (phiṭ) — fit (in good shape)}

\label{lesson:BN-C522-phit}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for yoga, then the Bengali for a strongman.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ফিট}}
\textbf{\bn{ফিট}} — \emph{phiṭ} — \textquotedblleft{}fit (in good shape)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{রোজ} \bn{হাঁটলে} \bn{তুমি} \bn{ফিট} \bn{থাকবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Roj hā̃ṭle tumi phiṭ thākbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you walk every day, you'll stay fit.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ফিট}} (\emph{phiṭ}) is borrowed from English \emph{fit}, used of health.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phiṭ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phiṭ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Roj hā̃ṭle tumi phiṭ thākbe.} — If you walk every day, you'll stay fit.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for yoga, then the Bengali for a strongman, then say \emph{phiṭ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{ফিট} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Fit (in good shape)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{বাঁকানো} (bā̃kāno)}{বাঁকানো (bā̃kāno)}]{\bn{বাঁকানো} (bā̃kāno) — to bend}

\label{lesson:BN-C522-bakano}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a strongman, then the Bengali for in good shape.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{বাঁকানো}}
\textbf{\bn{বাঁকানো}} — \emph{bā̃kāno} — \textquotedblleft{}to bend\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ব্যায়ামের} \bn{সময়} \bn{আমি} \bn{হাঁটু} \bn{বাঁকালাম।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Bæyāmer sômôy āmi hā̃ṭu bā̃kālām.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I bent my knees during the exercise.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{হাঁটু} \bn{বাঁকালেন}, \emph{tini hā̃ṭu bā̃kālen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{বাঁকানো}} (\emph{bā̃kāno}) is the verb of \bn{বাঁকা}, \textquotedblleft{}crooked\textquotedblright{}, from Sanskrit \emph{vaṅka}, \textquotedblleft{}bent\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 11191): to make something crooked.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bā̃kāno}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bā̃kāno}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Bæyāmer sômôy āmi hā̃ṭu bā̃kālām.} — I bent my knees during the exercise.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a strongman, then the Bengali for in good shape, then say \emph{bā̃kāno} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{বাঁকানো} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To bend\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{কুস্তি} (kusti)}{কুস্তি (kusti)}]{\bn{কুস্তি} (kusti) — wrestling}

\label{lesson:BN-C522-kusti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for in good shape, then the Bengali for to bend.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{কুস্তি}}
\textbf{\bn{কুস্তি}} — \emph{kusti} — \textquotedblleft{}wrestling\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{গ্রামের} \bn{মেলায়} \bn{কুস্তির} \bn{প্রতিযোগিতা} \bn{হল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Grāmer melāy kustir prôtijogitā hôlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There was a wrestling competition at the village fair.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{কুস্তি}} (\emph{kusti}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{kushtī}, \textquotedblleft{}wrestling\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}
